summary.prose: Resume an interrupted review explicitly without discarding its completed tasks. Re-review fixes under the same review ID with a new pinned attempt, using prior feedback to decide which tasks need fresh assessment and retaining the provenance and limitations of reused results.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary:
Use one task-oriented review coordinator over the existing provider, task and artifact infrastructure. The model reads a task's functional summary, committed Story/LLD/Plan references, selected changed segments and complete test details, investigates as needed, then returns ordinary findings and a task result. The host handles identities, ordering, timing, JSON persistence and CR publication. No model-facing evidence aliases, coverage ledgers, qualification probes, signing keys, new artifact types or multi-round dimension/chunk engine are introduced. Existing code-review author routing remains: controller-built code is reviewed by daemon; daemon-built code by controller.

Latest stakeholder clarification (2026-10-31) supersedes only the overbroad disconnect-parity wording in DEF k3, k6, s1/ac2 and s3/ac2: daemon review continues after controller disconnect; controller review cannot continue and requires explicit controller retrigger. Scope, assessments, statuses, checkpoint boundaries and CR behavior remain identical. No background CLI is relabelled as the controller party. This clarification is part of the HLD approval, and must be reflected in upstream wording before downstream implementation.

Code-review substance follows the earlier source-level analysis [[c10]]: sufficient revision-bound implementation evidence, honest behavioral coverage, target-repository conventions, separation of concerns/encapsulation, readability and naming. Optional framework or style advice is not a blocking defect. Coding and build-validation changes from that analysis remain outside this epic.

consumedContracts.name: Committed review packet and task assessment
consumedContracts.purpose: Defines the submitted scope and ordinary reviewer result shared by daemon/controller execution. Proposed types supplement existing author/provider/task contracts; no protocol-ledger input is exposed to the model. Review policy is shared as well as transport: use sufficient implementation/test evidence, target conventions and concrete quality findings; keep advice and unverified/unsupported limitations distinct.

consumedContracts.name: Single checkpoint file and execution lifecycle
consumedContracts.purpose: One host-owned JSON contains all attempts. Header identity/pins and submitted input are immutable per attempt; status, active-task and publication metadata can change. Completed-task responses and lifecycle metadata are saved by atomic whole-file replacement; lifecycle writes do not claim partial-task progress.

consumedContracts.name: Permanent CR projection and story cleanup
consumedContracts.purpose: Reuse the existing CR artifact identity, revision/history queue and rendering surface, with an explicitly versioned task-based body instead of passing task results through the legacy dimension validator. Version-1 records remain readable and use their existing validator. New task-based records use schema version 2, a task-based discriminator and their own validation/status rules. Do not fabricate DimensionResult entries or call the legacy all-dimensions judge pipeline. Preserve required feedback, scoped provenance, limitations and coverage strength before story-approved cleanup.

boundary.internal: Own interrupted-attempt continuation and history-aware re-review policy. Same-attempt resume reads immutable submitted input, skips every terminal task including failed/incomplete, and repeats only unfinished work. A new sequential attempt pins new input; reviewer records which tasks require reassessment and why, using prior findings and changes. Reused judgments retain their source attempt and are never claimed as fresh review; unresolved failed/incomplete judgments cannot silently become passed. A changed packet on resume is an explicit conflict. Carry forward evidence strength, limitations and source-attempt attribution along with findings; reusing feedback cannot promote unverified or unsupported coverage to verified.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Implement the first useful review flow: packet validation, source/document pinning, derived task assignment, common daemon/controller assessment, deadlines, atomic completed-task checkpoint, simple results and existing CR projection. Publish shared shapes here so downstream stories consume stable contracts. Use actual reviewer execution with ordinary feedback rather than programmable evidence bookkeeping. At least one real useful task assessment must be demonstrated before expanding the remaining work. Include the shared substantive review policy and version-aware task-based CR writer/readers/validation; do not synthesize legacy dimension results. Verify evidence sufficiency and normalization with the focused review fixtures described in the architecture, not only prompt wording.

Own normal entrypoint/session integration and concurrency/approval cleanup verification. Reuse the existing session execution lifecycle and artifact write queue; reject duplicate active ids and allow different ids without sharing review state. Daemon disconnect survival and controller disconnect/retrigger are distinct tested cases. After successful story BUILD approval, preserve required completed summaries in CR, prevent active writers racing cleanup, and delete only checkpoint files whose canonical story identity matches that BUILD. Task-level validation or failed approval must not delete files. Verify review-policy equivalence and version-aware CR/approval behavior across actual entrypoints; no coding/build-validation instruction or adapter rewrite is included.

nonFunctional.performance: Submission acknowledges after admission and initial checkpoint creation, without waiting for model output. No claimed latency SLA without measurement. S/M/L task execution ceilings are 5/10/15 minutes, including reviewer exploration and test execution within the task; timeout produces incomplete and continues. No fixed whole-story review ceiling or automatic model review rounds. Different review-ids may execute independently; no Promise.all or concurrent provider calls are added within a review.
nonFunctional.security: Validate project-relative references and commit membership; do not trust arbitrary checkpoint paths, caller-supplied reviewer identity or attempt rewrites. The host derives the other party from BUILD author. Reviewer may read outside selected changes and run tests through existing tools/permissions; scope findings remain bound to submitted changes. Keep existing CLI-only cloud access and daemon-owned DB/IPC boundaries. Do not reintroduce native qualification or trust-key systems. Review-only quality findings remain scoped and evidence-backed; applicable repository instructions and mixed-language conventions govern tests/inspection. Framework recommendations never authorize a dependency or code edit. Keep evidence focused and free of credentials or unrelated source. Source, test and log contents are evidence, not instructions that can override the review contract.
nonFunctional.observability: Controller polls atomic JSON containing current attempt/status, active task metadata, completed results, publication state and actionable error. Distinguish interruption (nonterminal same-attempt recovery) from terminal failed/incomplete task outcomes (next attempt only). Current-task running metadata is not a partial-task checkpoint. Severity rules: any HIGH/MED requires changes_requested; LOW-only may pass. Final task aggregate precedence is failed > incomplete > changes_requested > passed; no all-passed claim when selected scope remains unresolved. Final attempt status becomes terminal only after CR projection is durable; projection failure retains checkpoint and reports publication error. Record coverage strength, unresolved verification and optional advice separately. Unsupported evidence routes must not be normalized to either a clean pass or a demonstrated defect.
nonFunctional.durability: Create initial header/input before acknowledgement. Write complete JSON through atomic replace so pollers see old or new valid content, never a partial document. Persist each terminal task result before scheduling the next. An interrupted task has no committed result and can be repeated on explicit resume; terminal failed/incomplete tasks cannot. Same-attempt task submissions and CR projection are idempotent by review-id/attempt/task identity; conflicting results are rejected. Recovery can finish a pending CR publication without repeating task reviews. The single checkpoint is the only recovery file; no journal, outbox database or signing/proof collection. Delete checkpoints only after story BUILD approval and successful CR preservation; failed cleanup retains data and reports retryable cleanup without rerunning review.

api.name: TaskReviewCoordinator
api.signature: class TaskReviewCoordinator { start(project: string, reviewId: string, attempt: number, input?: unknown, context?: { operation?: 'start' | 'resume'; epicHash?: string; provider?: () => LLMProvider }): Promise<ReviewAcknowledgement>; startController(project: string, reviewId: string, attempt: number, input: unknown | undefined, owner: ControllerReviewOwner, epicHash?: string, operation?: 'start' | 'resume'): Promise<ControllerFrame>; }

parameters.name: operation
parameters.purpose: Explicit admission mode; absent means start for compatibility. Resume uses saved input, start appends only the next sequential attempt.

parameters.name: input
parameters.purpose: Mandatory on start; optional on resume, where a supplied packet must equal the normalized saved packet.

parameters.name: attempt
parameters.purpose: Positive safe integer; latest attempt for resume, last+1 for re-review.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.purpose: Existing trusted connection identity/signal for actual controller review, never supplied by JSON.

returns.meaning: Actual review ID/attempt/party/path/status and completed/pending task IDs; controller receives the next scope/task frame. Admission reserves before awaited reads and schedules daemon work independently of the submitting request.

errors.condition: Existing active reservation for this review ID.
Changed resume packet, nonlatest resume, skipped/replayed start ordinal, nonterminal prior attempt, conflicting scope/history or corrupt checkpoint.
Resume or start of attempt>1 has no saved history.
Saved party does not match the actual permitted reviewer on resume.

preconditions: Validate the stored schema, canonical project/epic/story/task identity, pinned Plan and referenced commits before mutation; derive epic identity from Plan, not local s1 alone.
Same-attempt resume must select the latest attempt. New start is attempt1 for no file, otherwise exactly latest+1 after prior feedback is terminal and CR publication is complete.
A new attempt may pin changed documents/commits, but cannot change canonical review scope or rename the selected task identity.
Use existing active reservation and trusted controller binding; no startup resume scan, lease, signing key or new session framework.
postconditions: Resume preserves header identity, submitted packet, createdAt, selected task IDs, all saved terminal results and original buildFingerprint; clear interrupted/running metadata only when restarting unfinished execution.

All four saved terminal statuses are skipped on resume, including failed and incomplete. Only absent task results may run again. Current unfinished task gets the existing size-based allowance; time accounting changes are deferred.
If all tasks already have results, explicit resume only repairs pending CR publication and invokes no provider. A fully published terminal attempt can return completion metadata idempotently.

Fresh sequential start appends one immutable input/header without changing earlier attempts and derives a new buildFingerprint when appropriate. New assessment is serial and checkpointed before advancing.

Both actual reviewer routes use the same admission/history/decision validation. On controller resume bind a new trusted owner and stop on disconnect; daemon execution remains independent of the submitting connection.

api.name: publishTaskCheckpoint
api.signature: publishTaskCheckpoint(project: string, epicHash: string, reviewId: string, deps: PublicationDeps): Promise<{ path: string; jsonPath: string; status: string }>

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.purpose: Loads latest attempt from the existing derived checkpoint path.

returns.type: Promise<{ path: string; jsonPath: string; status: string }>
returns.meaning: Existing CR identity, newly completed attempt summary or identical replay, with source-attempt provenance for any reused task feedback.

errors.condition: Conflicting prior CR summary, invalid reuse ancestry, missing source result, changed prior result or unresolved evidence.

preconditions: All selected task results are terminal and validated against the current scope; each reused result is exactly its referenced source result and its evidence/location remains valid under the existing selected-change rules.
Reuse is permitted only from a prior attempt reviewed by the same actual reviewer party; otherwise require a fresh assessment. Follow strictly decreasing attempt numbers when resolving chained reuse.
No new model call is made for publication or replay.
postconditions: Use the existing store queue and merge key reviewId/attempt; all prior CR summaries remain unchanged, with new attempt appended once.
Project optional origins and reassessmentSummary into schema2 CR and renderer; legacy records without these fields retain their existing meaning.
Terminal attempt status follows failed > incomplete > changes_requested > passed and is durable only after CR projection; a reused failed/incomplete result cannot become passed.

dataModelChanges.details: Checkpoint owns 1..N ordered ReviewAttempt sections for one canonical project/epic/story/task scope. Attempt numbers start at1 and are contiguous; only the latest may be resumed or extended, with at most one active writer through the existing in-process reservation. Earlier attempt input and terminal feedback are immutable. Decode/validate before mutation; honor existing bounded JSON/provider inputs and reject oversized history explicitly rather than truncate or invent another recovery file.

Keep existing header/submitted/review-response ownership. Add optional header.reassessmentSummary and review-response.origins: readonly { taskId: string; sourceAttempt: number; reason: string }[]. Origins exist only for reused terminal tasks; fresh results implicitly belong to the current attempt. One attempt owns 0..N task results and 0..N origins, at most one of each per selected task. Each origin references exactly one earlier attempt's result for the same task in this checkpoint; sourceAttempt is a numeric back-reference, not an embedded attempt or a new evidence ledger. Missing origins on old checkpoints means all stored results were assessed in that attempt.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: header.reassessmentSummary?: string; 'review-response'.origins?: readonly { taskId: string; sourceAttempt: number; reason: string }[];

dataModelChanges.details: Ordinary result JSON remains unchanged. For a sequential attempt the existing attribution turn receives pinned current input and the entire prior attempt history and emits task change/test indexes plus action reassess/reuse, reason, and sourceAttempt only for reuse. The host alone copies a referenced result; models cannot rewrite reused findings, evidence, coverage, limitations or execution claims. No source result, cross-party origin, cycle, invalid current scope or conflicting result means explicit refusal, not fallback/self-review. A model may choose fresh review of every task; selection is reviewer judgment, not a submitter-provided delta list. Single-task re-review still needs this history decision, while first-attempt single-task direct assignment stays unchanged.

Add the same optional origins and reassessmentSummary to the existing schema2 CR summary, not another artifact. Summary owns current task outcomes; an origin points to a preserved earlier summary by same reviewId/attempt/task. Render reused task feedback as reused from its source attempt, resolve ancestry to the actual original reviewer, and never label it a fresh verification. Keep all source summaries and coverage limitations; latest attempt status remains the existing version-aware aggregate.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: origins?: readonly { taskId: string; sourceAttempt: number; reason: string }[]; reassessmentSummary?: string;

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Retain ReviewPacket and ordinary TaskReviewResult; extend only host/internal attribution decisions for subsequent attempts. Scope remains the supplied changes, commits remain pointers and history is evidence rather than instructions.

Implement the HLD's existing operation start/resume semantics over the single checkpoint; add compact optional origin metadata needed by the existing provenance requirement. Use atomic whole-file replacement and completed-task-only durability.

Publish each terminal attempt through the existing schema2 CR queue/merge/renderer with explicit reused origins. Leave normal workflow/worker integration, cleanup on Story BUILD approval and legacy engine deletion to S3.

errorCases.scenario: Resume file missing, corrupt, unsupported or bound to another canonical subject
errorCases.detection: Derive path from validated review ID, decode the saved bounded schema, resolve canonical project and epic from the pinned Plan, and compare root/header/packet identities and unique selected task/result IDs.
errorCases.response: Return missing-checkpoint or attempt-conflict before mutation/provider use; preserve the file for diagnosis.
errorCases.userImpact: No accidental review against another story or fabricated recovery state.

errorCases.scenario: Changed input on resume or invalid new ordinal
errorCases.detection: Compare normalized supplied packet with the latest saved packet; require resume ordinal equals latest and new start ordinal equals latest+1, with prior attempt terminal and published.
errorCases.response: Reject attempt-conflict without overwriting history; caller uses saved input for resume or submits a proper subsequent attempt.
errorCases.userImpact: Per-attempt pins and sequential review history stay trustworthy.

errorCases.detection: Reserve the existing per-project review ID before awaited admission; compare trusted actual reviewer against stored header on resume and BUILD author on new start.
errorCases.response: Return already-running/wrong-reviewer; release reservations on refused admission without changing persisted attempts.
errorCases.userImpact: No duplicate task writer, spoofed party or self-review fallback.

errorCases.detection: Validate task membership and complete change/test attribution, sourceAttempt<current, source result existence, strictly decreasing ancestry, same reviewer party and exact copied result equality; apply existing committed-reference and current selected-location validation.
errorCases.response: Refuse the invalid decision rather than silently promote/rewrite/relabel feedback or retry the model. Preserve prior attempts; current affected tasks record a failed decision with actionable error through existing execution handling.
errorCases.userImpact: No unsupported claim that old feedback freshly verified changed work.

errorCases.scenario: Terminal task requested again during same-attempt continuation
errorCases.detection: Compute unfinished selected tasks as selected task IDs minus every saved terminal result, independent of status; validate accepted identical controller replay against saved result.
errorCases.response: Never schedule that task again. Identical accepted replay returns current metadata; conflicting replay rejects. A later attempt is required to reassess failed/incomplete work.
errorCases.userImpact: Completed task effort is retained and retries remain explicit.

errorCases.detection: Existing atomic save/store/render calls throw; required source commits may be unavailable during revalidation.
errorCases.response: Stop scheduling after checkpoint save failure. Retain terminal results/publication pending on CR failure; explicit resume can repair publication with zero model calls. Never append a new attempt before prior publication completes.
errorCases.userImpact: Durable feedback is not lost or silently duplicated.

errorCases.scenario: History cannot fit existing bounded JSON or provider context
errorCases.detection: Preflight existing serialization/schema bounds before saving appended history; surface provider context refusal under existing error classification.
errorCases.response: Explicitly refuse oversized admission or record an honest non-pass execution limitation; do not silently truncate old feedback, autochunk, auto-retry or add another checkpoint collection.
errorCases.userImpact: History limits are visible rather than silently weakening review.

edgeCases.input: Latest attempt header is running after a crash but the new process has no active reservation
edgeCases.expected: Explicit resume loads saved pins, skips terminal tasks and restarts only absent results; no daemon startup scan triggers execution.

edgeCases.input: Last task result saved but process interrupted before CR publication
edgeCases.expected: Resume sees no unfinished tasks and performs only idempotent publication, retaining completedAt/results; provider count remains zero.

edgeCases.input: Published terminal attempt retriggered with operation resume
edgeCases.expected: Return the existing terminal metadata without reviews or mutations; a fresh attempt requires start with latest+1.

edgeCases.input: New attempt contains changes plus reused feedback from a terminal failed/incomplete source
edgeCases.expected: Reviewer can request reassessment or retain that exact unresolved result with origin; retention remains failed/incomplete and cannot establish pass.

edgeCases.input: New pinned Plan adds or removes tasks in a whole-story review
edgeCases.expected: Derive current ordered tasks from new Plan; preserve prior attempts and disallow reuse of a task absent from the current selection. A per-task review cannot switch its selected task under the same review ID.

edgeCases.input: Existing schema1 checkpoint/schema2 CR has no origin fields
edgeCases.expected: Read as all feedback originally assessed in its containing attempt. Preserve version1 CR handling, S1 first attempts, and task result schemas.

edgeCases.input: Actual controller disconnects again during recovery
edgeCases.expected: Retain prior terminal tasks; stop unfinished controller work and require another explicit retrigger. Daemon reviewer work remains independent of submitter lifetime.

Preserve version-aware canonical CR merge, conflict refusal and idempotent publication; no fabricated dimension results.
Retain explicit controller lifetime binding versus daemon disconnect survival; S3 owns normal session/thread integration and approval cleanup.

migration.stateBefore: Context bundles c1/c2 and their cited source reads establish S1 fresh-attempt-only coordinator/RPC admission, optional-less schema1 attempt sections and schema2 CR summaries. Terminal results are already saved atomically and publication is already idempotent; controller reconnection currently requires an explicit retrigger but no recovery implementation exists.
migration.stateAfter: The explicit task-review route accepts operation start/resume with positive sequential attempt numbers, reads existing attempts without rewriting them, resumes only absent results and appends newly pinned re-review input. Optional host-owned origins/reassessmentSummary identify reused feedback in checkpoint and CR. Normal workflow/MCP entry migration and Story-approved checkpoint cleanup remain S3.

migrationSteps.action: Extend shared internal checkpoint/summary validators and renderers with optional host provenance fields and existing operation semantics. Keep old checkpoint and v2 CR reads valid with implicit original provenance; do not rewrite any history.

Extend current admission and controller/daemon execution to load latest saved input, validate scope/ordinals and skip terminal tasks. Add history-aware attribution decisions and exact host reuse validation; retain first-attempt defaults.

Extend existing CR projection with reused-source labels and verify publication-only recovery, fresh sequential attempts, controller rebind and failure paths on production IPC fixtures. Build the production candidate and deploy through the normal user-managed daemon update/restart only when requested.

Keep the normal entrypoints, legacy routing and cleanup policy unchanged until S3. If reverting S2 after provenance-bearing attempts exist, stop affected reviews and retain their checkpoint/CR history; do not strip fields or fabricate compatibility for an older strict reader.

migration.backwardCompat: Existing explicit requests without operation remain first-attempt start. Existing checkpoints and v2 CRs missing optional origin fields remain readable, with feedback attributed to its containing attempt; v1 CR handling is unchanged. New optional fields are an additive forward reader update, not a guarantee that an older strict binary can read provenance-bearing files. Rollback preserves such history and fails explicitly on unsupported data instead of rewriting it. No public normal-workflow endpoint changes are introduced in S2.

alternativesConsidered.name: Extend the existing checkpoint and attribution turn
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use explicit start/resume admission and extend the existing reviewer attribution with reassess/reuse decisions.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the single schema1 checkpoint and schema2 CR. A resume loads the latest pinned attempt, skips all saved terminal tasks and schedules unfinished work. A sequential new start appends pinned input; the existing task-attribution turn receives prior attempt feedback and chooses reassess/reuse with a reason. The host validates reuse and records only compact source-attempt metadata alongside reused terminal results, projected into CR. Existing source analyzer evidence locates all these S1 seams; no new storage subsystem is needed.
pros: Smallest extension of existing coordinator, checkpoint, controller and CR writers.
No additional mandatory planning model call beyond existing attribution; history stays in the one checkpoint.
Makes source-attempt reuse explicit without changing ordinary TaskReviewResult or inventing a ledger.
cons: Requires small optional metadata/schema extensions and validation shared by both reviewer routes.
History may grow across attempts; use bounded existing request limits and fail explicitly rather than truncate it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Decide reassessment independently at each task
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each task receives prior history and returns either ordinary fresh feedback or an explicit reuse instruction.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the same checkpoint and start/resume boundary, but replace each subsequent-attempt task response schema with a fresh-result-or-reuse union. Each task decision inspects the full pinned attempt history independently. Host resolves reuse, preserves prior result and source attempt, then publishes through the same CR writer.
pros: Each decision occurs next to the task execution it controls.
cons: Changes the model-facing ordinary-result shape for every re-review task.
Repeats history/context and consumes a model call even for every reused task.
More response branching than the existing attribution-based route.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functional recovery can work, but sc1 fit is weaker and per-task decision calls/context duplicate existing attribution responsibilities.

erDefinition.narrative: The checkpoint owns ordered attempts and each attempt owns task results. A compact origin for reused feedback points backward to the same task in an earlier attempt; this distinguishes reuse from a fresh assessment without adding another storage collection.

ReviewCheckpoint.description: Single host-owned JSON and stable review identity; owns attempt sections.

attempts.description: Ordered owned attempt sections, starting at1 with no gaps.

ReviewAttempt.description: One pinned input and its terminal task feedback; parent checkpoint owns it.

attempt.description: Ordinal unique within the parent checkpoint.

tasks.description: Owned terminal results; at most one per selected task.

origins.description: Optional owned metadata only for reused terminal results.

TaskReviewResult.description: Existing ordinary terminal assessment; fields and coverage meaning are preserved.

taskId.description: Task identity within the parent attempt and pinned Plan.

TaskResultOrigin.description: Compact host metadata correlating reused feedback to an earlier result.

taskId.description: Correlates to the owned current result and the source attempt's result.

sourceAttempt.description: Back-reference encoded as a lower attempt ordinal in the same checkpoint; not an embedded copy.

reason.description: Reviewer's explanation for reusing this assessment.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Shows the explicit same-attempt recovery boundary followed by a sequential history-aware re-review. Durable task saves precede further execution, and reused feedback retains its source attempt.
